c2-job-0016: Job 28 asks where wisdom can be found, and that is a question worth chasing. Let's read Job 28:1.
c2-job-0017: Job reminds us that God alone understands the way to wisdom. Let's look at Job 28:8 and 23 together.
c3-job-0018: God knows exactly where wisdom dwells, even when we cannot find it. Let's look at Job 28:26 and 23 together.
c3-pro-0020: Wisdom takes her stand up high and calls out to everyone who passes by. Let's read Proverbs 8:15 and 8:2.
c3-ecc-0005: The Preacher searched for just the right words, upright words of truth. Let's open Ecclesiastes 12:12 and 12:10.
c3-job-0019: Job and Proverbs both go looking for wisdom in high and hidden places. Let's read Job 28:7 and Proverbs 8:2.
c3-pro-0021: Job tells how iron is taken from the ground and copper is smelted from ore. Let's open Proverbs 8:34 and Job 28:2.
c3-ecc-0006: Near the close of Ecclesiastes the Preacher sums up his teaching, and Job says God understands wisdom's way. Let's read Ecclesiastes 12:11 and Job 28:23.
c3-job-0020: God will bring every deed into judgment, even the secret things. Let's check Job 28:18 and Ecclesiastes 12:14.
c3-pro-0022: The Preacher pondered, sought out, and set in order many proverbs. Let's read Proverbs 8:22 and Ecclesiastes 12:9.
c2-pro-0023: Proverbs opens by telling us why these sayings were collected for us. Let's turn to Proverbs 1:6.
c2-pro-0024: Proverbs 30 brings us the sayings of a man named Agur. Let's read Proverbs 30:1 and 29.
c3-pro-0025: Proverbs warns never to rob the poor or crush the afflicted. Let's read Proverbs 22:20 and 22.
c3-pro-0026: The LORD Himself will plead the cause of the poor. Let's turn to Proverbs 22:25 and 23.
c3-pro-0027: A king's mother urges him to judge righteously and stand up for the poor and needy. Let's check Proverbs 31:8 and 9.
c3-pro-0028: Agur notices creatures that are stately in walk, and he finds lessons all through creation. Let's read Proverbs 30:24 and 29.
c3-pro-0029: Agur humbly admits he lacks a man's understanding. Let's read Proverbs 30:28 and 2.
c3-pro-0030: Proverbs was written so we may know wisdom and instruction. Let's dig into Proverbs 22:21 and 1:2.
c3-pro-0031: Proverbs promises that finding wisdom brings a hope that will not be cut off. Let's read Proverbs 24:13 and 22:22.
c3-pro-0032: Solomon's proverbs open the book, and near its end Agur offers one more piece of counsel. Let's read Proverbs 30:32 and 1:1.
c2-hos-0009: Hosea prophesies while Uzziah sits on Judah's throne and Jeroboam on Israel's. Read Hosea 1:1 with me.
c2-jol-0005: Joel's book is short, but it rings with a call to return to the LORD. Let's read Joel 1:1.
c3-jon-0010: Jonah's story famously carries him out to sea and inside a great fish. Let's read Jonah 1:1.
c3-nah-0004: Nahum's message brings comfort to Judah and warning to Nineveh. Let's go to Nahum 1:1.
c3-zep-0006: Zephaniah prophesies while Josiah rules Judah. Let's read Zephaniah 1:1.
c3-oba-0004: Obadiah's vision closes with the kingdom belonging to the LORD. Let's read Obadiah 1:1.
c3-mic-0010: Micah's prophecy concerns Samaria and Jerusalem. Let's look closely at Micah 1:2.
c3-hab-0005: Habakkuk brings his honest complaint straight to the LORD. Let's read Habakkuk 1:4.
c3-jol-0006: Joel describes a locust swarm that devoured crop after crop. Let's read Joel 1:2.
c3-jol-0010: Joel calls the priests to wear sackcloth and cry out to the LORD. Let's look at Joel 1:3 together.
c2-zep-0011: Zephaniah sounds an alarm, yet his book ends with the LORD rejoicing over His people with singing. Let's read Zephaniah 1:15.
c2-jol-0007: The LORD gives voice before His army, for His camp is very great. Let's read Joel 2:5 and 11.
c3-amo-0010: Amos pronounces woe on those who long for the LORD's coming, asking what good it will do them. Let's open Amos 5:19 and 18.
c3-zep-0007: Amos asks whether it will not be very dark, with no brightness in it. Let's read Zephaniah 1:16 and Amos 5:20.
c3-jol-0008: At the close of his warning, Joel asks who can endure the LORD's coming. Let's read Joel 2:7 and 11.
c3-amo-0011: Amos calls for justice to run down like water, and Joel points to the strong One who executes His word. Let's turn to Amos 5:26 and Joel 2:11.
c3-jol-0009: Joel promises that the LORD will pour out His Spirit on His people. Let's read Joel 2:21 and Amos 5:20.
c3-zep-0010: Zephaniah warns that the LORD's great reckoning is near and hastens quickly. Let's read Zephaniah 1:17 and 1:14.
c3-mal-0005: Joel promises that God's people will eat in plenty and never be put to shame. Let's check Malachi 4:3 and Joel 2:26.
c3-amo-0012: Amos says the LORD takes no delight in empty feasts, and Joel calls Him the strong One who executes His word. Let's read Amos 5:27 and Joel 2:11.
c2-isa-0028: Isaiah pictures the Branch from the stem of Jesse, on whom the Spirit of the LORD rests. Let's read Isaiah 11:5.
c2-isa-0029: Isaiah speaks of the remnant of Jacob turning to the Mighty God. Let's dig into Isaiah 10:20 and 21.
c3-mic-0011: Micah foretells a Ruler coming out of Bethlehem. Let's read Micah 5:11 and 5:9.
c3-zep-0008: The LORD promises to save the lame and turn shame into praise. Let's read Zephaniah 3:18 and 19.
c3-zec-0009: Zechariah calls God's people to speak truth to their neighbors. Read Zechariah 8:10 and 16 with me.
c3-isa-0030: Isaiah pictures a highway for the remnant of His people. Let's read Isaiah 11:11 and 16.
c3-mic-0012: The LORD promises to bring His people together as sheep in the fold. Let's read Micah 2:13 and 12.
c3-zep-0009: The LORD will leave a meek and humble people who trust in His name. Let's go to Zephaniah 3:20 and 12.
c3-zec-0010: The LORD promises to return to Zion and dwell in the midst of Jerusalem. Let's read Zechariah 8:5 and 16.
c3-isa-0031: Isaiah compares Israel's people to the sand of the sea. Let's read Isaiah 11:15 and 10:22.
c2-1ki-0019: Israel's throne passes through several rulers in quick succession in this chapter. Let's look closely at First Kings 16:21.
c2-1ki-0020: Elah ruled Israel only briefly from Tirzah. Let's read First Kings 16:24 and 16:8.
c3-1ki-0021: Zimri struck down Elah and took the throne. Let's read First Kings 16:23 and 10.
c3-2ki-0021: Jehoash took Israel's throne after Jehoahaz. Let's look at Second Kings 15:13 and 13:10 together.
c3-2ki-0022: Second Kings 15 races through a string of short, troubled rules over Israel. Let's read Second Kings 15:23 and 14.
c3-2ki-0023: The LORD let Hazael king of Syria oppress Israel. Let's read Second Kings 15:27 and 13:3.
c3-2ki-0024: Azariah, also called Uzziah, ruled Judah for many years. Let's open Second Kings 15:5 and 13:10.
c3-2ch-0007: As long as Uzziah sought the LORD, God made him prosper. Let's read Second Chronicles 26:9 and 5.
c3-2ch-0008: Jotham built fortresses in the forests of Judah. Let's read Second Chronicles 26:15 and 27:4.
c3-2ch-0009: Jotham ruled in Jerusalem for sixteen years. Let's turn to Second Chronicles 27:6 and 8.
c2-ezr-0008: The LORD stirred up the spirit of Cyrus to let His people go home and rebuild. Let's read Ezra 1:8.
c2-neh-0009: Nehemiah served wine to King Artaxerxes and had never been sad in his presence before. Let's read Nehemiah 1:1 and 2:1.
c3-neh-0010: The king asked Nehemiah how long his journey would be, and he agreed to let him go. Let's check Nehemiah 2:8 and 6.
c3-est-0008: Mordecai was second only to King Ahasuerus and spoke peace to all his countrymen. Let's read Esther 1:1 and 10:3.
c3-est-0009: Esther's story ends with Mordecai seeking the good of his people. Let's read Esther 3:7 and 10:3.
c3-est-0010: Mordecai sent letters to all the Jews, near and far. Let's dig into Esther 9:31 and 20.
c3-hag-0005: Haggai urges the people to give careful thought and rebuild the temple. Let's read Haggai 1:1 and Ezra 1:6.
c3-zec-0011: Ezra records the platters and knives returned for the temple. Let's read Zechariah 1:1 and Ezra 1:9.
c3-zec-0012: Malachi delivers the LORD's word to Israel in the last book of the prophets. Read Zechariah 1:5 and Malachi 1:1 with me.
c3-ezr-0009: Neighbors were to help with goods, livestock, and freewill offerings for God's house in Jerusalem. Let's read Ezra 1:11 and 1:4.
